main_text.p: Argum. l.2.§. fin, D.de Donat.tia, quæ aliter effet præstanda, patri sit debita. Cessante enim legis causa cessat ipsa lex. Quinimo, si patria solvitur potestas, modo parens ad inhonesta tendat, incestuosas nuptias contrahat; cur non eodem jure, si non majori, patri aliquid erit detrahendum, si quando hostili in patriam est animo. Novell. 12[?], c.2.3. Patri quidem parendum est, cujus sancta persona filio, sed tamen patriæ magis est parendum, quæ nobis dulcissima, sanctissima. Neque enim unquam obediendum patri turpia imperanti, aut con-Gell. noct. Att. libr. s.cap.7.tra patriam.

4. Objicitur. Filius qui patris necem ultus non est, ut indignus hæreditate paternâ privabitur. Ergo multo minus l.1. Cod. de Indign.vitæ patris præjudicabit. Resp. Nulla est illatio, nulla consequentia. Ex officio tenetur filius, patris non jure occisi ne-cem

page.notes: The first word "tia" is a fragment carried over from the previous line. Two marginal notes are set in the left margin; the second is a bare reference. The printed "Novell." note reads "t2" in the scan, read here as 12 with a query. The first note, "s.cap.7.", is printed in the top left margin beside the first line. The note "l.1. Cod. de Indign." is printed in two lines in the left margin; the second line reads "deIndign.", which I have read as "de Indign.".
